sections.h2: Who records deeds in Jackson County, Michigan?
sections.html:
The Jackson County Register of Deeds records deeds, mortgages, land contracts and related papers for every parcel in the county. The office sits at 120 W Michigan Ave, 12th Floor, in the city of Jackson, and the county site lists weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. with the counter open through the lunch hour. Call 517-788-4350 before you drive in, because the office closes on all legal holidays.

If you are selling a house here, the register of deeds is the last stop in the sale. The title company or your attorney normally carries the signed deed to this office, pays the recording and transfer tax charges, and gets the recorded copy back for the buyer. Knowing what the counter will accept helps you spot problems before closing day.

The county covers 702 square miles of land according to Wikipedia, and its only city is Jackson, the county seat. Villages include Brooklyn, Concord, Grass Lake, Hanover, Parma and Springport, plus part of Cement City. A deed for a lot in any of them is recorded at the same counter in the city of Jackson.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Jackson County?
sections.html:
The recording fee is a flat $30 per document, no matter how many pages the deed runs. The county fee page says this flat rate has applied since October 1, 2016, and that a $4 survey remonumentation charge is already inside the $30. State law sets the amount in MCL 600.2567.

Other charges depend on what you hand the clerk. The county lists these items on its statutory fee page:

  • $3 for each extra instrument when one document assigns or discharges more than one mortgage or other instrument.
  • $1 per page for copies of real estate records and $5 to certify a copy.
  • A $5 minimum for a grantor and grantee search, which works out to 50 cents for each year searched.
  • $3 per name for a state or federal tax lien search.

The office takes cash, checks and credit cards. Make recording checks payable to the Register of Deeds, and add the transfer tax to the same check if the county tells you the tax is due at the counter.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Jackson County home sale?
sections.html:
Transfer tax in Jackson County is 55 cents per $500 of price for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, which together make $4.30 per $500 or fraction of $500. The Jackson County transfer tax page lists both rates, and the seller or grantor owes the tax. The county rate is set in MCL 207.504, and the state act puts liability on the seller in MCL 207.523.

The deed has to show the full price on its face, or you file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit with it. The affidavit carries no filing fee, but the deed must say that an affidavit is being filed. Any exemption you claim has to be written on the face of the deed as well.

Here is a worked example using the Census median value for owner occupied homes in the county, $193,700. Rounding up to $194,000 gives 388 blocks of $500, and 388 times $4.30 comes to $1,668.40 in combined transfer tax. Your own figure depends on the real sale price.

sections.h2: Which Jackson County sales skip the transfer tax?
sections.html:
Several transfers are exempt, and the exemptions come from state law rather than local custom. Both acts exempt instruments where the price is under $100, deeds given as security, and transfers between spouses that create or end a tenancy by the entireties. Foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure are exempt from the state tax under MCL 207.526.

The state act also exempts a conveyance from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child, and from a grandparent to a grandchild. The county act, MCL 207.505, lists a shorter set, so a family transfer can be exempt from one tax and still owe the other. Ask the register of deeds how a particular deed will be treated before you sign.

If you paid tax on a deed that later proves exempt, the state act lets the seller, or a buyer who paid on the seller's behalf, ask the Department of Treasury for a refund.

sections.h2: Does a Jackson County deed need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
Yes, when the deed carries a covenant of warranty. Warranty deeds, land contracts, and assignments of land contracts with a warranty clause need a certificate from the county treasurer before the register of deeds will take them. The rule is in MCL 211.135, which asks for proof that taxes on the parcel are paid for the five years before the date of the deed.

Jackson County charges $5 for the certificate, paid by a separate check made out to the Jackson County Treasurer and handed in with the recording. A quitclaim deed with no warranty language falls outside this rule under the same statute.

If you owe property tax on the house, ask the county treasurer for a payoff figure before the closing date so the title company can pay it from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What makes a deed acceptable at the Jackson County counter?
sections.html:
The deed must meet the page, ink and signature rules in MCL 565.201. The county reposts that statute on its Recordings page, and the register of deeds will return a document that misses any item. These are the points that cause most rejections:

  • Pages between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches, printed in black ink on white paper of at least 20 pound weight, in 10 point type or larger.
  • A blank margin of at least 2.5 inches at the top of the first page and half an inch elsewhere.
  • The kind of document named on the first line of print, and only one recordable event per instrument.
  • Each signer's name printed under the signature, a notary name printed on the same page as the notary signature, and the grantee's address shown.
  • The name and business address of whoever drafted the deed.
  • Social security numbers cut to the last four digits or removed.

The FAQ page adds that only documents with original signatures can be recorded, so a photocopy of a signed deed is turned away. Court documents need the court seal, and a death certificate needs the clerk's seal. The office does not prepare documents or supply forms, so use a title company or an attorney.

sections.h2: How do Jackson County housing numbers affect a sale?
sections.html:
Jackson County is mostly owner occupied, which keeps most sales in the ordinary buyer and seller category. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table shows 159,552 residents in mid 2025, 69,801 housing units, and an owner occupied rate of 75.0 percent. Median monthly owner costs run $1,377 with a mortgage and $557 without one, while median gross rent is $985.

  • Median value of an owner occupied home: $193,700 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median household income: $66,073 in 2024 dollars.
  • People aged 65 or older: 21.5 percent, a share that often means estates and downsizing sales.
  • Land area: 701.9 square miles, with about 228 people per square mile.

Older owners, inherited houses and homes needing work are common reasons sellers here look for a quick sale. If a title problem or unpaid tax is slowing yours, the register of deeds record is where it will show up.

sections.h2: How can I look up a recorded deed in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Start with the online grantor and grantee name search on the county Register of Deeds page, or go to the office with the legal description of the property. The county's FAQ says copies can be printed from the website or picked up in the office, and a title insurance policy often answers questions about easements or lake rights without a records search.

The office also offers a free property alert. Owners sign up and get notice when a document is recorded under a matching name, which helps catch a forged deed. If you spot a recording you never signed, call the register of deeds and local law enforcement.

When you want a seller's help with a title problem, bring the recorded deed, the mortgage payoff and any lien notices to the first conversation. Those three records tell a buyer most of what they need to price the sale.

faqs.q: Is the Jackson County recording fee based on page count?
faqs.a: No. The fee is $30 per document regardless of pages, and it has been since October 1, 2016. Extra instrument charges of $3 apply only when one document assigns or discharges several instruments.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when I sell my house in Jackson County?
faqs.a: The seller pays. State law makes the grantor liable, and the county collects both the 55 cent and $3.75 per $500 amounts when the deed is recorded, unless an exemption written on the deed applies.

faqs.q: Can I record a photocopy of my signed deed in Jackson County?
faqs.a: No. The register of deeds records only documents with original signatures. Court orders must carry the court seal, and death certificates must carry the clerk's seal.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate to record a quitclaim deed in Jackson County?
faqs.a: Usually not. The certificate requirement in MCL 211.135 covers deeds with a warranty covenant and land contracts, and quitclaim deeds with no warranties are excepted. Your title company can confirm for your deed.

faqs.q: What hours is the Jackson County Register of Deeds open?
faqs.a: The county lists Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., with the office open through lunch and closed on legal holidays. The phone number is 517-788-4350.
